At_3CHm_.md.category_evidence: A completion-stage meditation instruction on severing the link of body and mind; the opening names it "སྒྲ་མཐར་གྱིས་པའི་བསམ་གཏན་སྐྱེ་བའི་རིམ་པ་རྫོགས་པའི་རིམ་པ" and the colophon calls it "རྫོགས་པའི་རིམ་པ་ཕྱོགས་གཅིག་ཏུ་བསྡེབས་པ".

At_3CHu_.md.category_evidence: A Vajraḍākinī (Vajravārāhī) sādhana: it sets out the maṇḍala, the deity and the mantra recitation ("སྟོང་དང་ཁྲི་དང་བྱེ་བར་བཟླས། །སྔགས་པས་དངོས་གྲུབ་ཐོབ་པར་འགྱུར"). The guide files sādhanas under Tantras.

At_3CHw_.md.category_evidence: A sādhana of the wrathful Mudgara-Yamāri ("ཁྲོ་བོ་ཐོ་བ་གཤིན་རྗེ་གཤེད་ཀྱི་སྒྲུབ་ཐབས"), with a protection wheel, seed-syllable generation and mantra recitation. The guide files sādhanas under Tantras.

At_3CI2.md.category_evidence: An empowerment rite in a four-gate maṇḍala ("སྒོ་མ་བཞིའི་དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་དུ་དབང་བསྐུར་བའི་ཆོ་ག"), covering how to draw the maṇḍala, place the vases and give the empowerment. Maṇḍala and empowerment rites go under Tantras.

At_3CI5.md.category_evidence: An empowerment rite in the maṇḍala of the eight great planets ("གཟའ་ཆེན་པོ་བརྒྱད་ཀྱི་དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་དུ་དབང་བསྐུར་བའི་ཆོ་ག"), with Vajravidāraṇa at the centre and closing bali and torma offerings. This is a tantric maṇḍala rite.

At_3CI6.md.category_evidence: An empowerment rite in the maṇḍala of the eight nāgas ("ཀླུ་བརྒྱད་ཀྱི་དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་དུ་དབང་བསྐུར་བ"): it draws the maṇḍala, recites the heart mantras and empowers with vase water. This is a tantric maṇḍala rite.

At_3CI7.md.category_evidence: The Vajravidāraṇa ablution rite ("རྡོ་རྗེ་རྣམ་པར་འཇོམས་པའི་ཁྲུས་ཀྱི་ཆོ་ག"). Vase accomplishment rests on a maṇḍala, and the text refers to "དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་ཆོ་ག་དང་དབང་བསྐུར་བའི་ཆོ་ག". It is a tantric ritual manual, not a recitation text.

At_3CI8.md.category_evidence: A cremation rite for purifying the dead, performed in the Vajravidāraṇa maṇḍala and done as a fire offering ("སྦྱིན་སྲེག་གི་ཆོ་ག་ལྟར་བྱའོ"). Maṇḍala rites and fire offerings go under Tantras.

At_3CI9.md.category_evidence: A rite for making tsha-tshas and stūpas from the remains of the dead, continuing the Vajravidāraṇa purification cycle. It uses the seed syllables "རཾ", "བཾ" and "ཡཾ", a mantra, and visualisation of the stūpas as the five families. This is tantric ritual.

At_3CIA.md.category_evidence: A rite for freeing someone from nāga-spirit affliction, done with the pride of Vajravidāraṇa. It prescribes ablution, empowerment, fire offering and mantra formulas ("གནོན་ན་ནཱ་ག་སྟཾ་བྷ་ཡ་ནཾ"). This is tantric ritual action.

At_3CFb_.md.category_evidence: A Hevajra sādhana ("དཔལ་དགྱེས་པ་རྡོ་རྗེའི་སྒྲུབ་ཐབས་རིན་པོ་ཆེའི་སྒྲོན་མ") for practitioners who have received empowerment, with the eight-faced Heruka visualisation and a protection circle. The guide files sādhanas under Tantras.

At_3CG6.md.category_evidence: An Akṣobhya sādhana ("མི་འཁྲུགས་པའི་སྒྲུབ་ཐབས") for someone "དམ་ཚིག་སྡོམ་ལྡན་དབང་ཐོབ་པས", with self-generation as the deity and a HŪṂ on a lotus and moon at the heart. The guide files sādhanas under Tantras.

At_3CGE.md.category_evidence: A verse praise of the wrathful king Acala that describes his iconography and promises siddhis to those who praise and practise him ("བསྟོད་དང་བསྒྲུབ་པ་རྣམས་ལ་གསོལ་བར་འགྱུར"). The guide files a praise of a tantric deity (At_3CFl_, Vajrayoginī) under Tantras. It could also go under Liturgy as a recited praise.

At_3CGI.md.category_evidence: The ritual for the Uṣṇīṣavimala dhāraṇī ("གཙུག་ཏོར་དྲི་མ་མེད་པའི་གཟུངས་ཀྱི་ཆོ་ག"). It covers making a maṇḍala, tsha-tshas, vases and offerings, then giving ablution to the sick, and ends with torma to the spirits. This is a kriyā-tantra dhāraṇī rite.

At_3CGL.md.category_evidence: A metrical praise of Tārā in homage verses ("སྒྲོལ་མ་ལ་ནི་ཕྱག་འཚལ་ལོ") with no ritual instructions. It is meant for recitation ("གང་གིས་ཁྱོད་ཀྱི་མཚན་བཟུང་ཅིང་། །བསྟོད་དང་བསྒྲུབ་པ་བྱས་པ་རྣམས"), so it goes with recited praises under Liturgy. Tantras, as a praise of a deity, is possible.

At_3CGS.md.category_evidence: Torma and gaṇacakra offerings in the Cakrasaṃvara context ("བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་བདེ་མཆོག་ལ་ཕྱག་འཚལ་ལོ"), including blessing the alcohol in a skull cup and generating oneself as the samayasattva. The prompt files torma rites and tantric rituals under Tantras.

At_3CGT.md.category_evidence: A short sādhana of the white Khecarī form of Vajrayoginī ("མཁའ་སྤྱོད་མ་དཀར་མོའི་སྒྲུབ་ཐབས"), visualised from the syllable HRĪḤ and holding a curved knife and skull cup. The guide files sādhanas under Tantras.

At_3CGU.md.category_evidence: A sādhana of the Six-Syllable Avalokiteśvara ("འཕགས་པ་ཡི་གེ་དྲུག་པའི་སྒྲུབ་ཐབས"), with refuge, visualisation and recitation of "ཨོཾ་མ་ཎི་...པདྨེ་ཧཱུཾ" and the hundred-syllable mantra. The guide files sādhanas under Tantras.

At_3CGV.md.category_evidence: A sādhana of Vajrapāṇi in blue garments, lord of the yakṣas ("ལག་ན་རྡོ་རྗེ་གོས་སྔོན་ཅན་གྱི་བསྒྲུབ་ཐབས"), with glosses on the wrathful deity's iconography. The guide files sādhanas under Tantras.

At_3CGW.md.category_evidence: An exposition of the meaning of mantra ("སྔགས་ཀྱི་དོན་འཇུག་པ"), written to refute the view that the Secret Mantra is not the Buddha's word ("གསང་སྔགས་ཀྱི་ཐེག་པ་བཀའ་མ་ཡིན་ཟེར་བས"). It is a tantric doctrinal instruction.

At_3CGX.md.category_evidence: An instruction on empowerment ("དབང་གི་མན་ངག") explaining the vase and the higher empowerments, from the water empowerment to the prajñā-jñāna empowerment. It is tantric instruction.

At_3CGY.md.category_evidence: A teaching on the thirteen tantric samayas that must be kept after empowerment ("དབང་བསྐུར་ནས་དམ་ཚིག་སྲུངས་དགོས་པས་དམ་ཚིག་བསྟན"), warning of vajra hell if they are broken. It is tantric instruction.

At_3CGZ.md.category_evidence: A maṇḍala offering to the guru and the yidam ("མ་འདལ་འབུལ་བ"), made after generating the chosen deity and blessing body, speech and mind with "ཨོཾ་ཨཱཿཧཱུཾ". It cites the Avalokiteśvara tantra and is tantric practice. Liturgy, as an offering practice, is possible.
